card.occupation: Part-time interior design consultant for a small residential design studio in Dulwich. She works about two short days a fortnight, mostly client consultations, mood boards and sourcing fabrics and furniture.
card.education_detail: BA in Fine Art from a university in Kumasi, Ghana. After moving to London she took a part-time diploma in interior design in her early thirties, then a few short courses in colour and lighting.
card.household: Lives with her husband Kwame, 56, a finance director at a housing association, in a three-bedroom Victorian terrace they bought in 2004. Their two children, a daughter of 26 and a son of 23, have both moved out. The daughter lives in Manchester and the son in a flatshare in Peckham. No pets.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Accra, Ghana, in a Fante-speaking family, and came to London at 25 to join Kwame, who was already working here. She has been a British citizen for over twenty years. She is Christian and attends a Ghanaian Methodist congregation in South London most Sundays, though she treats it as much as community as worship. She speaks Fante and Twi with family and English everywhere else.
card.professional_persona: Calm and unhurried with clients. She is good at reading what people actually want under what they say they want. She steers clients towards pricier, better-quality pieces without them feeling pushed, and she is not above mentioning that she has done a house 'for someone quite well known' when it helps. She likes the part-time arrangement because it keeps the work interesting rather than a grind.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, round Brockwell Park most mornings, and does a Pilates class once a week at a studio on Railton Road. She watches the Ghana national team when there's a tournament on, mostly because Kwame does.
card.arts_persona: This is her main interest. She goes to the Dulwich Picture Gallery and the South London Gallery regularly and has a Tate membership. She follows contemporary African artists closely and has bought a couple of small pieces herself. She also reads widely, mostly literary fiction and design history.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Ghana every year or two, usually around Christmas. She prefers small, characterful hotels to big resorts and plans trips around galleries and markets: Lisbon, Marrakech, Copenhagen. Kwame does the bookings; she does the itinerary.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Ghanaian food at home most weeks, especially light soup, jollof and kontomire stew, but is curious and will try anything. She likes eating out somewhere a bit special and notices the interiors as much as the food. She calls the evening meal dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: Browsing antique and vintage furniture shops
card.career_goals: No big ambitions to expand. She would like to take on a few private clients of her own alongside the studio work, ideally period-house renovations, and perhaps one day help curate a small exhibition of Ghanaian design.
card.voice: Measured, low-key and fairly quiet, with a soft Ghanaian lilt underneath decades of South London English. She speaks at an even pace and thinks before answering, often starting with 'erm' or 'well'. She uses 'sort of' as a hedge now and then and sometimes ends with 'you know'. Her tone is polite and warm without being effusive. She is comfortable with silence and will simply wait, or say 'let me think' rather than fill the gap. She rarely raises her voice or gets animated, except a little when talking about art.
card.typing: Types in proper sentences with capitals at the start and correct apostrophes. She often skips the full stop at the end of a short answer. No text-speak, and she rarely uses exclamation marks. Answers are brief and to the point.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and pleasant at first, a little hard to read. She is polite, listens well and doesn't overshare. She comes across as composed and quietly confident, sometimes slightly cool, but kind if you need help or get something wrong. She warms up noticeably if the conversation turns to art, design or Ghana.
small_things: The Pilates teacher keeps changing the class time
A lovely mid-century sideboard she spotted in a shop in Crystal Palace
Her son never answers his phone
The rain has been relentless this week
She's halfway through a novel her book-loving friend recommended
Church harvest is coming up and she's been roped into decorating
deeper_things: She gave up a more serious painting career when the children were small and sometimes wonders what she'd have made of it
She finds the gap between how she's treated as a Black woman in some upmarket shops and how her clients treat her quietly funny, and uses it to her advantage
Her mother in Accra is getting frail and she is weighing how much time to spend there
She doesn't feel especially devout, and goes to church mostly for the people and the singing
She enjoys being comfortably off and doesn't feel guilty about it
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, camera slightly below eye level. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She is a Black woman in her early fifties with a calm, closed-mouth half-smile and steady eye contact with the camera. Her short natural hair is neatly shaped and greying at the temples. She wears tortoiseshell reading glasses pushed up on her head, small gold stud earrings and a loose mustard-yellow linen shirt. Behind her is a sage-green painted wall with a framed abstract print in ochre and indigo, a tall white shelf holding art books and a few handmade ceramic vases, and a trailing pothos plant on the top shelf. The edge of a brass floor lamp is visible on the right.
